text:
jen: Heads-up — target publish for py/ts SDK v2.3.0 in change-window-2 today at 2026-03-20 19:00 UTC. Main actions: canary publish, cut final tag, deprecate sync-client v1 in docs, and pin legacy shim in docs. @sam @maria please ack.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled publish job queued for 2026-03-20T19:00:00Z. CI checks pending (unit / integ / docs).

sam: Ack. Running final smoke now. I saw one lint failure in the ts build earlier — fixed on branch release/fix-exports and pushing the last commit.

ryan: Quick note: release notes must include explicit breaking note for rename ApiClient -> Client plus a short migration snippet.

maria: Can we avoid yanking the previous wheel? We have customers who pin. Plan: do not yank; mark deprecated in docs and add a clear migration section in release notes.

jen: Agreed. We'll add a deprecation notice to README and highlight the change in the changelog. No yanking.

sam: Confirming canary publish targets: TestPyPI for Python and npm dist-tag for TS. Commands I'm going to run: ```bash
python -m build && twine upload --repository testpypi dist/* && npm publish --tag canary-release-2026-03-20
```

deploy-bot: CI: unit tests passed; integration flaky tests skipped. No infra incidents. Canary publish allowed.

leo: Pin strategy: after successful canary we cut final with npm tag 'latest' and upload wheels to PyPI (no yank). We'll also add a soft-deprecation banner for sync-client v1 on docs.redwood.ai.

maria: Rollback plan: if post-release errors exceed 5% 5xx rate on SDK routes within the first 30m, revert npm tag and republish previous tarball (we have artifacts). For Python, PyPI won't let us yank reliably — we'll publish v2.3.1 with revert and mark v2.3.0 as problematic in the docs.

sam: :thumbsup: artifact storage keys ready. Canary publish in ~5m from my side.

jen: Running final checklist now: update release notes, update docs, tag release. @ops-bot please open an incident if metrics spike above thresholds.

ops-bot: ops-bot: alerts subscribed for this release. Thresholds configured: >2% errors OR tokenization regressions flagged in acceptance tests.

ryan: Added migration snippet for release notes: ```py
from redwood import Client  # replace ApiClient
```

maria: Also adding a deprecation header to the package homepage on PyPI linking to the migration guide.

jen: Publishing canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary published to TestPyPI and npm tag 'canary-release-2026-03-20' at 2026-03-20T19:00:42Z. Links: https://testpypi.example.org/project/redwood-sdk/2.3.0-canary and https://www.npmjs.com/package/redwood-sdk/v/2.3.0-canary

sam: Smoke on canary passed. No obvious runtime issues in internal staging.

leo: If nothing shows up in the next 10m we'll cut the final publish and promote npm tag to 'latest'.

maria: I'm publishing the deprecation section on the docs site now.

jen: Plan to cut final at 19:12 UTC if all clear. Monitoring enabled — thanks everyone.
